sections.overview: Lepisma saccharina is a wingless insect in the zygentome family Lepismatidae, familiar from human buildings as the silverfish.
sections.identification: Its flattened, tapering body bears silvery scales, long antennae and three slender tail filaments; adults reach about 15 millimetres.
sections.habitat: It shelters in dark, cool, humid places indoors and also occurs in natural leaf litter.
sections.diet: It consumes starch-rich material, mould and other detritus, and may damage paper, book bindings and some fabrics.
sections.behavior: It is mostly active at night and runs rapidly when exposed.
sections.reproduction: It develops without larval metamorphosis: juveniles resemble adults and continue moulting as they grow.
sections.ecology: The firebrat Thermobia domestica is a close household relative, but favours warmer sites than the cool, damp microhabitats typical of silverfish; it has no profile here.
sections.conservation: A French regional atlas reports the species throughout France; those local occurrence records are not a global population assessment.
